Technical SEO & AI Search Engineering Glossary.

Definitive reference guide covering Entity-Attribute-Value (EAV) modeling, Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), RAG chunking, and modern search engine mechanics.

AI Search

Answer Engine Optimization (AEO)

The practice of formatting and structuring website content to be selected as the primary source in conversational AI answers, including Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, and ChatGPT Search.

Engineering Context

Focuses on explicit entity definitions, concise 40-word answer spans directly below H2/H3 tags, and structured schema grounding.

Read Deep-Dive Framework →
Technical SEO

Canonicalization

The technical method of specifying which URL represents the master copy of a webpage using rel='canonical' tags, preventing duplicate content penalties across dynamic or filtered query strings.

Engineering Context

Crucial on large Shopify and programmatic catalogs where identical products exist under multiple category hierarchies.

Read Deep-Dive Framework →
AI Search

Citation Share of Voice (C-SoV)

The percentage of AI-generated answers for a specific prompt cluster that cite a particular brand or domain relative to all cited competitor domains.

Engineering Context

Replaces traditional SERP position tracking in zero-click and generative search environments.

Read Deep-Dive Framework →
Technical SEO

Core Web Vitals (CWV)

Google's standardized user experience metrics measuring real-world web performance: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), Interaction to Next Paint (INP), and Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS).

Engineering Context

Poor CWV scores deplete Googlebot crawl frequency and negatively impact algorithmic ranking weights.

Read Deep-Dive Framework →
Technical SEO

Crawl Budget

The volume of requests search engine spiders (like Googlebot) are willing and able to execute on a website within a given timeframe without overloading the host server.

Engineering Context

Waste occurs when bots spend requests fetching faceted navigation, duplicate search queries, or broken redirect loops instead of revenue pages.

Read Deep-Dive Framework →
Architecture

Directory Consolidation (301 Migration)

The deliberate structural consolidation of fragmented, thin subfolders or orphaned blog posts into unified authoritative topic hubs via permanent 301 redirects.

Engineering Context

Protects overall domain threshold value and eliminates internal page cannibalization in post-core-update environments.

Read Deep-Dive Framework →
Quality & YMYL

E-E-A-T (Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, Trust)

The quality benchmark used by Google Search raters and algorithmic quality systems to evaluate whether content creators and domains possess genuine real-world authority.

Engineering Context

Mandatory in medical, financial, and legal verticals. Grounded via Person schema, professional credentials, and editorial policies.

Read Deep-Dive Framework →
Semantic Architecture

Entity-Attribute-Value (EAV) Model

A knowledge graph data model representing concepts as distinct Subject (Entity) -> Predicate (Attribute) -> Object (Value) triples, allowing search engines and LLMs to understand relationship context.

Engineering Context

Elevates content beyond flat keyword repetition into verifiable semantic nodes that withstand search engine algorithm updates.

Read Deep-Dive Framework →
AI Search

Generative Engine Optimization (GEO)

The engineering discipline of preparing digital ecosystems for consumption, retrieval, and attribution by generative artificial intelligence models and large language models (LLMs).

Engineering Context

Combines /llms.txt deployment, high-density entity summaries, and deterministic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) structures.

Read Deep-Dive Framework →
Technical SEO

Googlebot JavaScript Rendering (SSR vs CSR)

The two-wave indexing process where Googlebot crawls raw HTML first, then defers JavaScript execution (CSR) until headless rendering resources become available.

Engineering Context

Server-Side Rendering (SSR) ensures critical internal links, product prices, and body copy are indexed instantly in the first wave.

Read Deep-Dive Framework →
Architecture

Keyword Cannibalization

A search architecture failure where two or more pages on the same domain compete for the exact same query intent, splitting authority and causing volatile SERP rankings.

Engineering Context

Resolved by merging competing pages into a master parent pillar or differentiating search intents through distinct EAV attributes.

Read Deep-Dive Framework →
AI Search

llms.txt Standard

A proposed web standard located at /llms.txt that provides a clean, machine-readable markdown index of a website's core entities, documentation, and authoritative pages specifically for AI crawlers.

Engineering Context

Eliminates HTML layout noise, navigation menus, and tracking scripts so LLMs ingest exact factual source context.

Read Deep-Dive Framework →
Technical SEO

Log File Forensics

Analyzing raw web server access logs to observe the exact timestamps, HTTP status codes, and user-agent frequencies of Googlebot and AI crawlers.

Engineering Context

The only source of truth for crawl behavior before data reaches Google Search Console reporting.

Read Deep-Dive Framework →
Architecture

Programmatic SEO

Building structured template-driven landing page architectures powered by a dataset (e.g., location pages, vehicle specs, directory entries) to capture long-tail search demand at scale.

Engineering Context

Requires strict unique value checks, custom attribute mapping, and indexing controls to avoid thin-content penalties.

Read Deep-Dive Framework →
AI Search

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)

An AI architecture that retrieves authoritative external document chunks matching a user prompt before generating the final conversational response.

Engineering Context

Search systems (e.g. Perplexity, ChatGPT Search) use RAG to cite websites. Content must be structured in cohesive 30-50 word answer chunks to avoid chunk pruning.

Read Deep-Dive Framework →
Semantic Architecture

Schema.org Graph (JSON-LD)

A machine-readable linked data markup format placed in <script type='application/ld+json'> tags that communicates entity relationships directly to search crawlers.

Engineering Context

Nested @graph schemas link Organization, WebSite, WebPage, Article, and Person into an interconnected knowledge web.

Read Deep-Dive Framework →
Semantic Architecture

Topical Authority

A search engine's assessment of a website's depth, breadth, and reliability across an entire knowledge domain, rather than on single isolated keywords.

Engineering Context

Achieved by systematically covering core concepts, adjacent subtopics, and practitioner questions in structured pillar-cluster networks.

Read Deep-Dive Framework →
AI Search

Zero-Click Search

A search query where the user's intent is fully satisfied directly on the search engine results page (via AI Overviews, Knowledge Panels, or Featured Snippets) without clicking through to any website.

Engineering Context

Requires brands to pivot from tracking raw impressions to optimizing for direct entity citation and mid-funnel consultative queries.
